outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Crypto, led by Bitcoin and Ethereum
strongest.reason: Bitcoin is up roughly 12% over two days as Trump and crypto industry executives make a final push for Congress to pass the Clarity Act, which would clarify whether digital assets are regulated as securities or commodities

strongest.area: AI/enterprise software, led by ServiceNow, Adobe, Oracle, and Salesforce
strongest.reason: BofA raised price targets across a batch of AI-exposed software names this week, and Oracle jumped sharply today, extending a broader recovery in software sentiment after months of AI-disruption fears

weakest.area: Chips and AI hardware, led by AMD, ASML, Arm, Cadence, and Synopsys
weakest.reason: the chip-stock rally hit a speed bump as elevated long-term Treasury yields pressured richly-valued growth names, even with a mixed Nvidia headline on a possible China AI chip return

weakest.area: Robotics and single-name cybersecurity, led by Intuitive Surgical, UBTECH, and CrowdStrike
weakest.reason: Intuitive Surgical's drop looks like an outsized move worth confirming, UBTECH cooled as capital rotated toward Unitree's blowout Shanghai debut, and CrowdStrike is pulling back from highs on profit-taking rather than new bearish news

outlook.nextStep: Nvidia's China AI-chip headline and its August 26 earnings report are probably the two most important things to watch for the chip and AI-infrastructure tiers over the next week. Today's crypto surge and the software-sector bounce are worth noting but are better treated as still-developing moves to watch confirm over the next few sessions than as settled trend reversals.

signals.title: Bessent threatens 'toughest sanctions in history' on Iran as yields stay elevated
signals.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US would levy the toughest sanctions in its history against Iran, helping lift futures and keeping a geopolitical premium in oil. Separately, the 30-year Treasury yield touched its highest level since 2007 earlier this week before easing slightly, and the Fed has now held rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% for multiple consecutive meetings with one 2026 cut still penciled in.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether elevated long-term yields keep weighing on richly-valued growth names into the September Fed meeting

signals.title: Chip-stock rally hits a speed bump as yields bite
signals.body: AMD, ASML, and Arm all traded lower today as a multi-week chip-stock rally cooled, with several analysts pointing to elevated long-duration Treasury yields pressuring expensive growth names rather than any single negative catalyst. Nvidia was choppy after a report it plans a modified, China-specific AI chip using licensed Groq technology, a headline that briefly lifted shares before gains were pared.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this is routine digestion after a strong run or a deeper valuation reset ahead of Nvidia's August 26 earnings

signals.title: Oracle jumps while megacap AI-infrastructure peers stay soft
signals.body: Oracle rose sharply today, a notable reversal after weeks of lagging its hyperscaler peers, while Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft all traded lower. Nvidia's reported plan to re-enter the China market with a modified AI chip underscores continued efforts to defend its AI infrastructure position even as competitors chip away at its lead.
signals.focus: worth watching whether Oracle's bounce holds or proves to be a one-day move relative to the broader infrastructure group

signals.title: BofA lifts price targets across AI-exposed software names
signals.body: Bank of America raised price targets on a batch of software companies including ServiceNow and Adobe, citing growing conviction that AI will be a net positive for the group rather than a disruptive threat, fueling a broader rally in software sentiment this week. ServiceNow rose again on the news.
signals.focus: worth watching over the next few sessions to see whether this analyst-driven optimism translates into a durable sentiment shift

signals.title: Bitcoin surges 12% in two days as Trump pushes final Clarity Act vote
signals.body: Bitcoin and Ethereum both jumped as Trump and crypto industry executives lead a last-ditch push for Congress to pass the Clarity Act before the current session winds down, which would settle whether digital assets are regulated as securities or commodities.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this translates into sustained institutional flows once (or if) the legislation actually passes, versus proving to be a headline-driven pop

signals.title: CrowdStrike pulls back from highs on profit-taking, not new bearish news
signals.body: CrowdStrike fell again today, but the move looks more like a cooling-off period after a run to fresh highs than a reaction to negative news — several analysts raised price targets this week and reiterated bullish ratings even as the stock slipped below its short-term moving averages. The pullback also follows the company's four-for-one stock split completed earlier this summer.
signals.focus: lower conviction on reading too much into the single-name pullback given the still-bullish analyst backdrop

signals.title: Unitree's 600%+ Shanghai debut redirects speculative capital in humanoid robotics
signals.body: Unitree, the world's largest humanoid robot maker by sales, saw shares surge more than 600% in its Shanghai trading debut this week, a sign of how much speculative capital continues flowing into the space. UBTECH cooled today, plausibly as some of that flow rotated toward the newer listing, while Teradyne held up despite a valuation-driven downgrade following its own strong run.
signals.focus: worth treating single-day swings in individual names as noise relative to the broader capital-flow trend into humanoid robotics
